    Meet Kiki Goti, Kelly Wearstler's pick for the most influential designer of the next 20 years

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1276 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dezeen

    ⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Next up in Dezeen’s 20×20 project in partnership with Kohler, which marks 20 years of Dezeen, is Greek designer Kiki Goti, who was nominated by Kelly Wearstler for her innovative approach to ornament and artisanship.
    • Goti has experienced a remarkable rise since presenting a furniture collection made from salvaged foam insulation during the 2023 edition of Milan design week.
    • Her conceptual, research-led work typically explores heritage, identity and craftsmanship, resulting in playful objects and spaces that reexamine the cultural codes embedded in design.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Next up in Dezeen’s 20×20 project in partnership with Kohler, which marks 20 years of Dezeen, is Greek designer Kiki Goti, who was nominated by Kelly Wearstler for her innovative approach to ornament and artisanship.

    Goti has experienced a remarkable rise since presenting a furniture collection made from salvaged foam insulation during the 2023 edition of Milan design week.

    Her conceptual, research-led work typically explores heritage, identity and craftsmanship, resulting in playful objects and spaces that reexamine the cultural codes embedded in design.

    Goti was nominated as an emerging talent to watch by American designer Wearstler, who praised how Goti “approaches ornament with the precision of an engineer and the instincts of a sculptor”.

    “That refusal to treat craft and technology as opposites is going to matter more over the next 20 years,” Wearstler added.

    As well as a shared love of ornament and the decorative arts, Wearstler also picked up on how Goti’s practice is informed by her background in robotics and machine learning.

    “It’s amazing to be nominated by such a major designer, and also someone who shares my passion for craft and attention to detail,” Goti told Dezeen.

    It’s amazing to be nominated by such a significant designer, and also someone who shares my passion for craft and attention to detail.

    Goti added that she was pleased to be recognised by a leading female designer, as her creative muses are mostly women and femininity plays a major role in her own practice.

    “My work is very personal so of course there are a lot of references to being a woman,” she said, adding that she draws inspiration from well-known artists and designers such as Louise Bourgeois and Faye Toogood.

    Goti spoke to Dezeen from Paris, where she currently lives with her partner, French filmmaker Vincent Staropoli, having recently relocated there from New York.

    She was raised in Thessaloniki and received a diploma in architecture from the local AUTh university before completing a masters degree in Integrative Technologies and Architectural Design Research at Stuttgart’s Institute of Computational Design.

    The move to Newly introduced York came after accepting a research position at Pratt Institute, but during the Covid pandemic Goti realised that she missed making her own work, so began experimenting with found materials.

    In a recent development, “I really didn’t know what I wanted to do,” she recalled. “But through my research at the university and the New York design community I realised there were other people working in a similar way, which encouraged me to stick with it.”.

    The initial collection was followed by projects made with glass, marble and, most recently, a series of furniture pieces featuring lacquered wooden surfaces that contrast with bell-like aluminium elements.

    Recent findings suggest that the outcomes are very unpredictable. Because the collections all look different there isn’t anything people can point to and say ‘that’s clearly made by Kiki’.

    Goti explained that her work usually starts with research into a specific technique or a material that interests her, before she then applies her findings to the design of an object.

    She noted she finds this approach creatively fulfilling as it offers endless opportunities, though as someone early in her career it means there is no identifiable style associated with her work.

    It has been revealed that “I don’t usually have a form or a shape in mind when I start,” she remarked. “So the outcomes are very unpredictable. Because the collections all look different there isn’t anything people can point to and say ‘that’s clearly made by Kiki’.”.

    According to recent reports, “In the long term I hope people will recognise my work because of its research-led approach,” she continued. “We need to take more time to understand other artists’ work and not judge everything based on a few images on social media.”.

    Decoration and ornamentation are recurring elements within Goti’s oeuvre, although she doesn’t want to be labelled as a maximalist.

    It has been revealed that “My work is sometimes very ornamental and sometimes it’s more minimal,” she added. “So there’s a gradient and the outcome is really determined by the process.”.

    Like many contemporary designers, Goti does not produce all of her own work, instead utilising a network of expert artisans to help bring her whimsical and deeply personal creations to life.

    “I’m a very collaborative person and I think we can create better outcomes when we put our minds together with other people,” she said.

    “My architecture background really helped me develop this collaborative mindset and I think one of the key things you learn as you get older is to be selective about who you work with.”.

    I’m a very collaborative person and I think we can create better outcomes when we put our minds together with other people.

    The collection she developed with Marble Sachanas (top) exemplifies this collaborative approach, applying Goti’s visionary and playful style to an ancient material sourced from a quarry close to her home town.

    Goti met the organization’s representatives during 2025’s Milan design week and struck up a conversation that led to them returning this year to exhibit the outcomes as part of the Alcova event.

    Projects such as the marble pieces and the furniture she developed for Mexican gallery Toro Manifesto fall into the category of collectible design, which Goti pointed out is a consequence of their artisanal production rather than a conscious decision to make high-end, limited-edition objects.

    According to recent reports, “Everything nowadays is so expensive to make,” she explained. “If you want to make something that’s well-crafted you have to pay for the materials, the shipping, the labour and that causes the price to be high – it’s not the designer’s fault.”.

    The armchair, coffee table and sideboard were shown at the Collectible design fair in Newly introduced York, but Goti remarked she would also be interested in working on designs that could be licensed and produced by a brand.

    She is currently developing a collection of glass objects that will be smaller and more affordable than her large-scale Graces vessels, while retaining their exuberant aesthetic.

    Alongside her personal projects, Goti also runs an interior design practice together with Staropoli called The House Special Studio, which combines her distinctive aesthetic approach with his cinematic vision.

    The studio’s first completed project was the renovation of a compact Paris apartment, which reflects their desire to create spaces that feel fun, personal and lived-in.

    Looking ahead to what the next 20 years might hold, Goti intends to continue experimenting with different materials and techniques, while attempting to document her design process in a more detailed and consistent manner.

    She believes some designers, herself included, have reacted to the isolated experience of Covid lockdowns by working more with their hands and exploring upcoming ways of collaborating, which she hopes will continue over the coming years.

    According to recent reports, “I feel we’re all craving crafts and handmade objects more than ever,” she remarked. “The more digital content we are fed, the more we are drawn back towards analogue experiences.”.

    It has been revealed that “I think we all want more physical interaction with materials and with each other, as well as more intimate settings where we can come together and make things. That’s the kind of future I want to see.”.

    Sources indicate that to celebrate Dezeen’s 20th birthday, we asked 20 of the most influential architects and designers of the last 20 years to identify someone they think will have a major impact in the next 20 years.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    There are many possible causes for bumps inside your nose — some as harmless as a pimple, others that might need more attention. It’s easy to imagine the worst, but the truth is usually less alarming.

    Like on your face, the pores inside your nose can become clogged with oil, dirt, and bacteria, leading to pimples. These can be painful and may swell, especially in such a sensitive area.

    It has been revealed that non-cancerous growths can develop in the nasal passages or sinus lining due to chronic inflammation, allergies, or infections. While they’re usually painless, larger polyps can cause blockages, leading to breathing difficulties, a reduced sense of smell, or recurrent sinus infections.

    Recent findings suggest that when you pluck or trim nose hairs, the hair can sometimes grow back into the skin instead of out, causing an ingrown hair. If this becomes infected, it can result in a painful bump inside the nose.

    A bump can also form inside the nose due to trauma, such as a blow to the nose, or even from something as simple as aggressive nose-picking. The trauma can cause the tissue to swell or become bruised. In some cases, a hard bump may form as the tissue heals.

    Fluid-filled sacs that can form in your nose, usually harmless but sometimes uncomfortable.

    A hard bump inside the nose might be due to problems with the cartilage, such as a deviated septum or cartilage overgrowth.

    Small, benign bumps that may appear on or in the nose are often mistaken for pimples but are fibrous tissue growths.

This ointment is applied directly inside the nose to target the infection, reduce redness, and promote healing.

    #172969. 7 Tips for Building a Healthy Diet With Canned, Frozen, and Packaged Goods

    📅 17 Apr 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1483 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Self ↗ Open Full Page

    7 Tips for Building a Healthy Diet With Canned, Frozen, and Packaged Goods

    📅 17 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1483 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Self

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that certain influencers have built entire social media empires out of making everything from scratch.
    • For the vast majority of people—meaning those who don’t make their living off of wellness content or have near-endless amounts of time and money to burn—canned, frozen, and packaged stuff is almost always a far more practical option.
    • Besides the lower price point, canned, frozen, and packaged foods have one other major advantage: their staying power.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that certain influencers have built entire social media empires out of making everything from scratch. Oftentimes, their videos carry an implicit sense of moral superiority, suggesting that you’re not a good parent (or at least not as good as them) if you’re resorting to pre-packaged store-bought items. Those who pick their own produce and painstakingly hand-craft their own candy necklaces simply work harder, love their children more, are fundamentally better.

    But this suggestion is hardly fair. For the vast majority of people—meaning those who don’t make their living off of wellness content or have near-endless amounts of time and money to burn—canned, frozen, and packaged stuff is almost always a far more practical option. “Groceries are a fortune,” after all, Anthea Levi, MS, RD, a Brooklyn-based health writer and the founder of Alive+Well Nutrition, tells SELF—and fresh items tend to be the most expensive, as a trip to the produce section of the supermarket will readily prove.

    Besides the lower price point, canned, frozen, and packaged foods have one other major advantage: their staying power. “You can keep them in your freezer for months, so that often gives people confidence” in the purchase, since they know they don’t have an expiration date hanging over their head, Desiree Nielsen, RD, a recipe developer with a focus on plant-based nutrition, tells SELF. This, in turn, leads to reduced food waste: “Fresh salad greens are notorious for going slimy in the fridge, but you’ll never have that issue with frozen spinach. Ditto for fish. Fresh fish needs to be cooked ASAP before it turns, while frozen fish and canned or tinned fish last until you’re ready to use them,” Levi says.

    Nielsen also takes problem with the basic idea that these options are somehow inherently inferior—“a substantial, big misconception,” in her eyes. “There has been a lot of confusion about the nature of these foods in general. Just because something is processed or packaged does not mean it’s unhealthy,” she says.

    In other words, canned, frozen, or packaged items are often perfectly fine to include in your diet—and you shouldn’t feel embarrassed, ashamed, or inadequate if they make frequent appearances in your meals (or if they’re your first resort over fresh). “Constant access to fresh foods is, unfortunately, a luxury. If canned, frozen, or packaged items are the only way you’re able to put a fruit or vegetable on your plate, go for it,” Levi says. But if you’re still concerned about the health aspect, there are a few key ways to maximize the nutritional value and improve the overall experience. Here’s what to know to make the most of your freezer stash.

    “Typically, the fewer ingredients, the better,” Levi says—a rule of thumb to consider while shopping. While canned, frozen, and packaged items have a reputation for being ultra-processed—rife with additives and lower in nutritional value—there are actually plenty out there “that are made from just one or two whole-food ingredients, such as canned peas, frozen fruit, and canned salmon,” Levi says. “These are as close to fresh foods as you can get, and just as nutritious.” Many jarred peanut butters only contain dry roasted peanuts and salt, for example. (By contrast, Ritz peanut butter crackers, which have an ingredients list several rows long, are a very different story.).

    That remarked, this issue can be nuanced. “Just because an ingredient looks fancy or technical or like a chemical does not necessarily mean that it's bad for you,” Nielsen points out. Many processed foods—including bread, milk, and breakfast cereal—are fortified with healthy vitamins and minerals that you might not otherwise consume enough of in your diet. Take vitamin C—which may appear under the name “ascorbic acid”—as an example. “You might not recognize that what you’re looking at is vitamin C, so you don't want to scare yourself off of potentially nutritious and valuable food because you see things on the ingredients label that you don't recognize,” Nielsen states.

    Sources indicate that in Nielsen’s experience, canned foods are often considered even less “healthy” than frozen, but the stigma isn’t necessarily warranted. Canned beans, which boast fiber, plant-based protein, and minerals like iron and zinc, are an excellent example of a canned food that amounts to an “incredible nutrition source,” she claims. Still, this category does have one major drawback: Staples like veggies, soups, and, yes, beans can contain a significant amount of sodium, a mineral that can cause high blood pressure and related challenges like heart disease and stroke when overconsumed. Tinned fish like TikTok’s beloved sardines can suffer from the same concern, as the brine inside the tin can be heavy on added salt as well.

    Given that many brands offer sodium-sensitive alternatives, try to prioritize those options instead to keep your sodium intake in check and avoid potential health consequences, according to Nielsen. Look for labels like “No salt added,” “Low sodium,” or even “No sodium” to steer you in the right direction. If you can’t find anything fitting that bill at your local store, draining and rinsing canned products before use can also drastically cut down on the sodium content—by up to 40%, according to some estimates. (Just keep in mind this method may also cause losses in other nutrients, like vitamin C.).

    “In terms of packaged and processed foods, I'm always looking for a couple of nutrients to minimize and a couple of nutrients to optimize,” Nielsen says. Sodium is one to limit or avoid, as we’ve already covered, but there are others too—like added sugars and saturated fat. “Peaches that come canned in sugary syrup aren’t as nutritious as peaches that come canned in water, or are purchased frozen or fresh,” for example, Levi says.

    It has been revealed that on the other hand, when you’re reading over a nutrition facts label, “what you want to see is fiber,” Nielsen states—and “protein is a significant bonus.” Multiple vitamins and minerals in a product is also often a positive sign. Even breakfast cereals, which are often thought of as unhealthy, “can be incredible sources of minerals like iron and zinc—things that we need that help to keep our metabolism running, that keep us energized,” Nielsen says.

    In a recent development, trying to decide between two (or more) similar products? Comparing and contrasting the ingredients can help you narrow it down, according to Nielsen. Take breakfast cereal: You’ll want to ask yourself, “‘Which one of these cereals gives me the most fiber, the most protein, has the least sugar?’” she claims. In this case, the relative content of vitamins and minerals can also be a helpful clue. Seeing that a cereal contains 10% to 20% of your recommended dietary allowance, as many do, can be “your sort of gut check that this is actually a really nutritious food,” Nielsen says.

    Recent findings suggest that even though frozen veggies are affordable and durable, they do have one big downside compared to fresh: Their taste and texture can take a hit—and, in turn, “you do have to adjust your cooking somewhat,” Nielsen indicates. To prevent sogginess, cook frozen veggies from frozen rather than letting them defrost first, according to Levi. And you’ll want to use heat-based cooking methods (like air-frying, baking, roasting, and stir-frying) “as opposed to water-based methods like boiling or steaming,” she says.

    “Many of us are working more than ever before—maybe working two or three jobs—and we don't have a lot of time to put a home-cooked meal on the table,” Nielsen indicates. Strategically pairing your canned, frozen, and packaged items is an easy way to boost efficiency in the kitchen without sacrificing nutritional value. If you’re having canned soup for dinner, you can dump in a can of lentils to boost the fiber and protein, for example. (Bonus tip: You can also use this approach to stretch out your leftovers. Need a batch of spaghetti to last longer? Toss some frozen peas on top or some frozen broccoli on the side.).

    Industry observers note that “Stocking your freezer and pantry with budget-friendly canned, frozen, and packaged items can help make balanced meals a breeze,” Levi claims. Follow the tried-and-true “plate method” to guarantee a nutritious result, according to Nielsen: Reserve a quarter of your plate for whole grains or starchy vegetables, another quarter for protein, and the remaining half for fruits and non-starchy veggies. You could make rolled oats with chia seeds, frozen berries, and peanut butter for breakfast, or pasta with tinned sardines and frozen broccoli for dinner, for example, Levi says. “It sounds way too simple, but it is backed by so much science to help you balance your diet without counting anything,” Nielsen says. “As long as you stick to that plate method, you will be eating a nourishing diet”—yes, even if your ingredients don’t come to you direct.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Photography by Gabriel Konrath.

    Contrasting volumes of smooth plaster and rough local Morelo stone define this coastal home in Brazil, designed by local architecture practice Ambidestro.

    Named Casa Los Cobos, the home is located in Xangri-Lá on Brazil’s southern coast, and was designed to make the most of panoramic views out over the sea from the rear of the site.

    Set back from the road, a series of routes both through and around the home “reveal the landscape gradually,” including a path beneath a timber canopy and via a paved veranda screened by lush plants.

    “The main opportunity was the merging of two adjoining lots into a single site that extends to the rear, where the landscape opens onto the water,” Ambidestro co-founder João Pedro Crescente told Dezeen.

    The ground floor of Casa Los Cobos has been given over almost entirely to a single large living, dining and kitchen space, wrapped by service spaces and bathrooms.

    Full-height sliding glass doors allow this space to be opened out onto a large sheltered terrace alongside a swimming pool, with a lawn that slopes down to a nearby waterway.

    “The ground floor is free of partitions: living, dining and the entertaining kitchen are integrated and turned toward the greenery, accommodating everything from a weeknight dinner to a Saturday party,” Crescente told Dezeen.

    Sources indicate that “Between the living room and the water lie, in sequence, the veranda, the garden and the pool, which wraps around the house. The eye passes through these layers before reaching the backdrop,” he added.

    Both the exterior and interior have been given contrasting finishes of rough Morelo stone and white plaster and paint, with the rear terrace framed by white-painted masonry.

    This is complemented internally with bespoke carpentry in pale oak, including a floating timber bar supported by a concrete column that defines one edge of the living space.

    “The intention was to use natural, local materials in light, warm tones repeated inside and out, making the transition between spaces almost imperceptible,” said Crescente.

    “Moledo stone clads the facades and changes in appearance from morning to late afternoon. Other natural stones continue onto the floors and wet areas,” he added.

    A skylit staircase leads up to the more compartmentalised first floor of the home, which contains six en-suite bedrooms, two of which open onto a balcony overlooking the sea.

    To provide both shading and privacy from the road, sliding timber shutters can be pulled down over the full-height bedroom windows.

    Other homes in Brazil recently featured on Dezeen include a home in São Paolo by Studio Arthur Casas featuring dramatic overhangs and cantilevers, and a low-lying dwelling by Sabella Arquitetura that is topped by a gridded timber roof.

    Photography by Gabriel Konrath.

According to the Foundation, more than 900 workers and artisans took part in ZHA's first completed project in Africa, and 90% of the construction was carried out by Moroccan companies that prioritized the local sourcing of materials and components. The photographs show the interplay of heights and volumes characteristic of Zaha Hadid's work.

    The building is organized around a canyon-like, triple-height foyer with interweaving staircases, which serves as the main circulation route and as a gathering space before and after performances. At the top of the staircases, above the foyer, a restaurant overlooks the river valley and the medina. The complex includes three performance venues: the Auditorium, a 1,821-seat opera theater; the Studio Theatre, an experimental performance and rehearsal space for 250 people; and the open-air Amphitheatre, which extends east from the main building and accommodates 7,000 spectators for large public performances and festivals.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Photography courtesy of Texas Space Commission.

    Industry observers note that the Texas Space Commission has published a proposal for the newly created United States Space Academy. It would be located in Houston on a site alongside NASA‘s Johnson Space Center, which was formerly home to Mission Control.

    Sources indicate that revealed earlier this week, the proposals show clusters of buildings arranged in a flower-like shape, with petals surrounded by water. The renders place the facility on a presently vacant site alongside the NASA facility.

    The proposal was created as a response to a request for information from the American space agency, which is looking to find a permanent home for the academy.

    It follows an executive order issued earlier this year by president Donald Trump that established a presidential commission to determine how the proposed NASA-led institution could be formed.

    In the order, he stated that the United States Space Academy would be established with the aim of training the “next generation of astronauts, scientists, engineers, operators, entrepreneurs, civil servants, and warfighters”.

    The proposed academy would contain facilities for academic and more hands-on training.

    It has received bipartisan support in Texas, with Republican senator Ted Cruz and Democrat senator-elect James Talarico issuing a joint statement in support of the bid.

    “Texas has maintained a leading role in America’s human spaceflight program for decades, from training astronauts to directing missions at Johnson Space Center,” noted the pair in the statement.

    It has been revealed that “The Lone Star State has developed an extensive space industry, infrastructure, and expertise. Texas is best suited to train the next generation of American space leaders and is the natural home for the U.S. Space Academy.”.

    According to the Texas Space Commission, the scheme was designed to align with NASA’s proposed timeline, which envisions groundbreaking commencing next year.

    NASA recently announced intends for a permanent moon base, with a multi-phased blueprint culminating in “semi-permanent habitation models”.

    Photography courtesy of Texas Space Commission.

    Public Architecture, Learning Environments, and Civic Life.

    Sources indicate that from educational facilities to community infrastructure, recent projects and recognitions highlight how architecture accommodates collective activities and responds to different social contexts. Scheduled to open in December, the 31,000-square-foot New Mexico Literacy Institute by Multistudio and Design Plus Architects brings together flexible learning spaces, reading nooks, recreational areas, and a central courtyard designed to accommodate more than 550 learners and educators, extending educational activities beyond conventional classrooms. In Mexico, COLECTIVO C733 was named the inaugural recipient of the Siza Award for Public Architecture, established by the Serralves Foundation to recognize socially engaged practices working with public space and local communities. The studio's portfolio includes markets, cultural facilities, transport hubs, parks, and public landscapes, among them Matamoros Market, Tapachula Station, and Bacalar Eco-Park, alongside projects developed with SEDATU in vulnerable communities. The award recognizes the studio's contribution to civic infrastructure and public space, bringing renewed attention to architecture's role in supporting shared spaces and community life.

    Colonial Urbanism and Indigenous Spatial Traditions.

    The Colonial City of Santo Domingo in the Dominican Republic offers a historical perspective on the development of urban planning in the Americas, tracing the formation of a settlement that became an early precedent for colonial urban structures across the region. Founded in 1496 and relocated to the western bank of the Ozama River following a hurricane in 1502, the city was reorganized under Nicolás de Ovando around a central plaza, a cathedral, and a regular street grid. Predating the Laws of the Indies of 1573, its layout represents an early example of planning principles later formalized across Spanish colonial settlements, while its two distinct centers around the main square and riverfront reflect the relationship between civic authority and commercial activity. The city's spatial history also raises questions about the influence of Indigenous settlement patterns, with research suggesting that the Plaza Mayor may have occupied the center of an earlier Taíno settlement organized around communal open spaces known as bateyes. This possibility offers another reading of colonial urbanism, in which the imposition of European planning systems may have also involved the appropriation and transformation of existing spatial structures.

    The Floating Cultural Center El Embarcadero / Natura Futura.

    Located along the San Pablo River in Babahoyo, Ecuador, the Floating Cultural Center El Embarcadero by Natura Futura introduces cultural and educational infrastructure to the Barreiro neighborhood, where residents lack access to public social and cultural facilities. Developed with REARC Practice Lab, local organizations, and the community, the project combines a floating cultural center with a floodable amphitheater, an open-air educational ring, and a mobile Canoe Library. Built on an approximately 10-by-16-meter platform, the center accommodates a library, community kitchen, educational spaces, and common areas. Its timber truss structure and split-bamboo roof respond to the local climate, while floating structures, floodable surfaces, and mooring systems accommodate seasonal changes in the river's water level. The Canoe Library extends the initiative to remote riverside communities, bringing books, workshops, and educational activities by boat. Through these interconnected spaces, the project approaches the river as an extension of the city's public realm and a setting for collective learning and cultural exchange.

    Visitor Center at La Hacienda Clase Azul / Elías Rizo Arquitectos.

    Sources indicate that located in Capilla de Guadalupe, in the highlands of Jalisco, Mexico, the 6,625-square-meter Visitor Center at La Hacienda Clase Azul by Elías Rizo Arquitectos draws on the traditional Mexican house and its central courtyard. Set between an agave landscape and an oak forest, the project comprises eight volumes connected by a portico and arranged around a central courtyard with a reflecting pool, forming a horseshoe-shaped plan that opens toward the surrounding landscape. The building accommodates a welcome hall, museum, store, bar, restaurant, and visitor experience spaces, while a basement houses the tequila cellar and service areas. The reflecting pool also provides thermal insulation for the cellar, while subterranean courtyards bring natural light and ventilation to the lower level. Rocks sourced from the site were processed and used throughout the building's walls, connecting its material expression to the surrounding terrain.

    Kaybé Tulum – Multisensory Park / Arquitectura Mixta.

    Located within a tropical jungle in Tulum, Mexico, Kaybé Multisensory Park by Arquitectura Mixta is an 800-square-meter landscape project organized around a sequence of sculptural bamboo structures and winding pathways. Commissioned as part of a low-density residential development, the park preserves much of the existing vegetation, allowing its architectural interventions to emerge within the surrounding landscape. The route connects several pavilions, each exploring different relationships between nature, perception, and the senses, including Toroides, an entrance structure formed by interlocking bamboo geometries; El Átomo, a multipurpose gathering space; and Torre Nikte, a flower-inspired lookout tower with a helical staircase. Bamboo is used throughout in different structural configurations, including laminated beams and woven elements, demonstrating its versatility in creating varied geometries while establishing a consistent architectural language across the park.

    Getty Introduces Conservation Project for Peru's 17th-Century Church of Rondocan.

    Industry observers note that the Getty Conservation Institute has declared a multi-year project to conserve the Church of Santo Tomás de Aquino, known locally as the Church of Rondocan, in Peru's Cusco region. The initiative, developed in partnership with the Dirección Desconcentrada de Cultura – Cusco, will address earthquake-related damage through seismic retrofitting and support the conservation of the 17th-century adobe structure and its collection of more than 300 cultural objects. The collection includes religious paintings, gilded wooden altarpieces, sculptures, and textiles, as well as eight paintings by Italian Jesuit artist Bernardo Bitti, a series previously thought to be lost. One of the paintings will be transferred to the Getty in 2027 for scientific analysis and conservation. Construction is scheduled to begin on site in 2027, with the regional cultural authority funding and carrying out the work while Getty monitors its progress.

    Bloomberg Philanthropies Expands Asphalt Art Initiative Across the Americas and Caribbean.

    Bloomberg Philanthropies has opened applications for a new edition of its Asphalt Art Initiative, which offers grants of US$100,000 to cities across the Americas and the Caribbean to transform streets into safer and more vibrant public spaces through art. Up to 10 cities will be selected to develop projects that reclaim street space for pedestrians, improve road safety, and create new gathering places, with technical support from Bloomberg Associates, Street Looks Collaborative, and TY Lin. An updated study examining more than 50 projects across the United States found a 52% reduction in traffic crashes involving pedestrians or cyclists, a 32% decrease in overall crashes, and a 55% decline in near-miss incidents involving pedestrians following the interventions. Previous projects include redesigned intersections in Puebla, Mexico, where average vehicle speeds decreased by 61%. Cities with populations of at least 50,000 can apply until February 11, 2027, with selected projects expected to be implemented in late 2027 and 2028.

    #172959. Breaking: How Taking a GLP-1 Could Affect Your Bone Health

    Breaking: How Taking a GLP-1 Could Affect Your Bone Health

    📅 19 Apr 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1586 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Self

    ⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • When it comes to treating obesity, type 2 diabetes, and other chronic health conditions, GLP-1 agonist drugs—such as Ozempic, Zepbound, and Wegovy—have been a game changer for literally millions of Americans.
    • Industry observers note that but as with any medication, these drugs can deliver unwelcome side effects.
    • It has been revealed that the research, which was presented at the 2026 American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons annual meeting in March and has not yet been peer-reviewed, found a link between GLP-1 use and increased risk of bone complications, including osteoporosis (weak, brittle bones) and osteomalacia (soft bones).
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    When it comes to treating obesity, type 2 diabetes, and other chronic health conditions, GLP-1 agonist drugs—such as Ozempic, Zepbound, and Wegovy—have been a game changer for literally millions of Americans.

    Industry observers note that but as with any medication, these drugs can deliver unwelcome side effects. And a recent study that just garnered a bunch of attention raised the possibility of fresh ones.

    It has been revealed that the research, which was presented at the 2026 American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons annual meeting in March and has not yet been peer-reviewed, found a link between GLP-1 use and increased risk of bone complications, including osteoporosis (weak, brittle bones) and osteomalacia (soft bones). The study also found a link between GLP-1 use and heightened risk of gout, a type of arthritis that causes pain and swelling in the joints.

    The lead study author said he became interested in whether GLP-1s might affect bone and other connective tissue after some of his patients “developed serious tendon tears following relatively minor injuries,” according to NBC News. After analyzing five years of medical records from nearly 147,000 adults with type 2 diabetes and obesity, the study authors concluded that GLP-1 use was associated with a “significantly increased” risk of osteoporosis, osteomalacia, and gout.

    Sources indicate that of course, this news is likely unsettling for anyone on these medications. But should we be legit worried about these findings? And how exactly could GLP-1s harm bone health in the first place? We tapped two experts for answers, along with practical tips for protecting bone health while taking GLP-1s.

    First, some relieving news: As of now, there is “no sound scientific evidence” that suggests GLP-1s directly increase the risk of osteoporosis or osteomalacia, Marci Laudenslager, MD, an obesity medicine physician with The Johns Hopkins Healthful Eating, Activity & Weight Program, tells SELF. (Same goes for gout, she adds.).

    It has been revealed that dr. Laudenslager, who was not involved in the study, points out that it was observational in nature, meaning it looked at correlation…not causation. “While well-conducted observational studies can reveal a potential relationship between a medication and a clinical outcome, they cannot determine whether a medication directly causes that clinical outcome,” she explains.

    It has been revealed that another limitation of the study is that it relied on medical records alone, which means it assumed that all patients who were prescribed GLP-1s, as noted in their medical records, were actually taking the drug. In reality, many patients who are prescribed GLP-1s are unable to take them because of cost or medication shortages, Dr. Laudenslager says. Moreover, people who do start taking don’t always continue due to insurance, cost, or problems tolerating the drug, she adds.

    According to recent reports, beyond that, the study didn’t take into account factors that commonly impact bone health, like exercise habits, nutritional habits, and other lifestyle factors, Kelyssa Hall, an exercise physiologist and certified strength and conditioning specialist at Hospital for Special Surgery, tells SELF. “These factors can play a huge role in bone health with or without the addition of GLP-1s.” The study also didn’t account for certain endocrine conditions, cancers, alcohol use, family history, and steroid use–all of which can also play a role in bone health, Dr. Laudenslager adds. And the study didn’t note which specific GLP-1 drug people used and the dosage, she adds.

    It has been revealed that lastly, the study findings have not yet been peer reviewed–a step that Dr. Laudenslager describes it as “essential” in the scientific process. As Hall puts it: The study “highlights the need for more research on these topics.”.

    According to recent reports, okay, so that particular study has its limitations. But other research supports the notion that these drugs may be linked with declining bone health. So…is there actual cause for concern?

    According to recent reports, according to Dr. Laudenslager and Hall, taking GLP1-s can indeed decrease bone density for some people. But that’s likely due to the volume and rate at which people lose weight while on these drugs—and not anything specific to the medication itself, Dr. Laudenslager says.

    Sources indicate that “When you take GLP-1s, there can be rapid weight loss which means there is less load being carried around on the skeleton,” Hall states. “Bone formation or strengthening is improved with load to the skeletal system,” she explains, “so losing weight decreases the regular load on the bones overall.”.

    Sources indicate that over time, this decrease in loading can translate to a decrease in bone density, Dr. Laudenslager notes. But, again, this isn’t unique to GLP-1s: “Significant weight loss through any mechanism—lifestyle change, medications, or surgery—can impact metabolism as a whole and bone metabolism, in particular,” she says. Basically, whenever you lose a bunch of weight—regardless of how you lost those pounds—there’s always a risk of bone loss.

    It has been revealed that in short, while it’s true that some people taking GLP-1s have had changes to their bone health, these changes seem to “be driven primarily by magnitude of weight loss rather than a direct, negative consequence of the medications themselves,” Dr. Laudenslager says. That remarked, the use of GLP-1s and bone health “is an active area of study,” she adds. More research is needed to fully understand the impact of GLP-1s on bone density.

    Resistance training is notable for pretty much everyone—and that includes folks on GLP-1s. One of its many benefits is that it’s been shown to improve bone density, Hall says. That means it can be a helpful strategy to bolster bone health when you’re on a GLP-1. Plus, strength training can help guard against muscle loss that can happen when you’re losing weight. “Retaining muscle mass is important for strength and stability,” she says. And it can also help support your overall metabolism, she adds, which can help your body sustain weight loss results for the long haul.

    According to recent reports, if you’re new to strength training, Dr. Laudenslager recommends gradually building up to a routine of two to three sessions a week, with at least a day off in between each workout to allow your muscles the time they need to recover. Before getting started though, make sure to check with your doctor or other medical provider so they can advise what type of workouts are safe and recommended for you.

    In a recent development, A common side effect of GLP-1s is appetite suppression, which can sometimes lead people to follow a really low calorie diet. Calorie restriction can suppress bone growth and increase the risk of fractures, according to research, which is one of the reasons you want to make sure you’re still eating enough to support your overall health while on a GLP-1. “Hunger is an essential hormonal cue we all need in order to sustain health,” Dr. Laudenslager notes. The ideal amount of calories is highly individualized, but if you’re unsure that you’re getting what you need, bring it up with your doctor or another qualified expert, such as a registered dietitian.

    Protein is often touted for its muscle-building benefits, but it’s also vital for bone health, as it helps to build bone mass. The recommended dietary allowance for adults is 0.8 grams of protein per kilograms of bodyweight a day—a general guideline that Dr. Laudenslager also suggests for people taking GLP-1s. She suggests a slightly higher intake for people at greater risk of bone health problems (such as older adults and postmenopausal women) and lesser amounts in people with kidney disease. Just make sure that as you prioritize protein, you don’t skimp on important components of a well-rounded diet, including fiber, water, healthy fats, and essential vitamins, minerals, and nutrients, she adds.

    According to recent reports, rapid weight loss can be harmful for bone health, so to mitigate this risk, strive for a more gradual reduction in pounds. The recommended rate of weight loss depends on your starting weight, but as a general guideline, Dr. Laudenslager recommends losing 5% to 10% of your total weight over the course of about six months. This translates to an average of about 0.5 to 2 pounds lost a week. So if you notice that taking a GLP-1 is causing you to lose weight at a faster pace, bring it up with your doctor. They may want to adjust your medication dosing to help slow your weight loss rate into a more ideal, gradual range.

    Sources indicate that bone loss isn’t an overnight thing. In fact, clinically significant bone loss typically happens over the course of years, Dr. Laudenslager indicates. “This means there are a wealth of opportunities throughout a person’s weight loss journey to prevent and treat bone loss early on if it’s detected through surveillance.” So if you have any bone health concerns, mention them to your doctor (though hopefully your provider is proactively thinking about this too).

    On that note, Dr. Laudenslager strongly encourages people interested in obesity treatment to seek care from a board-certified obesity medicine physician. She recommends the American Board of Obesity Medicine and the Obesity Action Coalition websites as resources for finding a board-certified provider.

    Industry observers note that GLP-1s can be a true game-changer for people struggling with chronic health conditions. Unfortunately, there’s still a lot of societal stigma and misunderstanding surrounding obesity, including the misconception that “anti-obesity medications are dangerous and should be avoided,” Dr. Laudenslager states. In truth, though? “The medication side effects are quite manageable when prescribed by providers who are well-versed in current practice guidelines,” she says.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Photography by Eron Costin.

    Brazilian firm Estúdio 41 has completed Guaratuba House, which features exterior screens and a structural system that “explores the architectural expression of exposed precast concrete“.

    Located in the seaside community of Prainha, which sits within the city of Guaratuba in southern Brazil, the holiday home was designed for a family to serve as “a refuge between the mountains and the sea”.

    “One of their main requirements was, therefore, a strong visual connection between the interior spaces and the surrounding natural landscape,” mentioned Estúdio 41, an architectural firm based in Curitiba.

    Sources indicate that rectangular in plan, the 375-square-metre house has two floors. It is wrapped in folding screens made of perforated melamine panels.

    Industry observers note that the screens filter natural light and reduce solar gain on glass surfaces. When opened up, they reveal views of the scenic landscape.

    “At night, the transparency and geometric patterns of the house’s skin give it the appearance of a lantern within the landscape,” the team remarked.

    To protect against flooding, as the coastal site has been affected by storm surges in the past, the building was lifted up 70 centimeters (2.3 feet).

    It has a prefabricated concrete structural system that was assembled in only six hours, with the concrete structural elements left visible.

    In a recent development, the system consists of six columns, four beams and 20 double-tee slabs, also known as “π” (pi)-shaped slabs. The latter are pre-stressed concrete panels with a cross-section that resembles the Greek letter π.

    “The project explores the architectural expression of exposed precast concrete,” noted the team.

    “The conception of a very simple and easily executable construction system reflects a concern for the realities of the local workforce,” it contniued.

    “The construction technique, the modular arrangement of the structural components, and the ribs of the double-tee floor slabs are all clearly legible.”.

    It has been revealed that rooms feature artful decor and a neutral colour palette. The ground level contains an open-strategy kitchen, dining area and living room, along with service areas and a guest bedroom.

    The communal area opens toward a garden, and beyond it, a sheltered barbecue terrace and a swimming pool.

    “The social areas were conceived as one large veranda in direct contact with the beach sand, with views of both the sea and mountains,” the team mentioned.

    The upper level contains four bedrooms, including the primary suite, and a family room. A bridge passes over the garden below and connects to a concrete terrace with sweeping views of the sea.

    Other projects by Estudio 41 include a small white house in Brazil with a roof garden, and a prefabricated, teal-coloured research station in Antarctica.

    In a recent development, unlike open coastlines or the edges of natural bodies of water, urban canals are narrow, linear, engineered landscapes that cut decisively through the urban fabric. Where rivers follow the contours of a landscape and shape the landform, canals impose their geometry and logic, redefining the relationship between architecture and water. Their edges are clearly defined, often shaped by retaining walls, embankments, and the infrastructure that supports movement along and across the water. Bridges, pedestrian walkways, mooring points, and docks establish a distinctive relationship between the waterway and its context, creating an urban environment where the boundaries between water and architecture are realized.

In some cities, people avoided these waterways altogether. Today, however, a growing appreciation for urban blue infrastructure is transforming canals' role in the city. Investments in waterway restoration, pedestrian accessibility, and public spaces are reintroducing canals as valuable environmental and social assets, shifting their identity from utilitarian infrastructure toward places of recreation and connection.

    Industry News: Programa extension brings SketchUp models and product schedules into one workflow

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (510 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dezeen

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Studio operations software Programa has introduced a SketchUp extension that connects 3D models with its product Schedules, freeing designers from duplicating information and giving them more creative time.
    • According to Programa, the extension is designed to reduce duplicate data entry by connecting a 3D model in SketchUp with a project’s Schedule in Programa.
    • Programa’s Schedules function acts as a streamlined alternative to spreadsheets, detailing each item’s code, supplier, finish, dimensions, quantity and price.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Studio operations software Programa has introduced a SketchUp extension that connects 3D models with its product Schedules, freeing designers from duplicating information and giving them more creative time.

    According to Programa, the extension is designed to reduce duplicate data entry by connecting a 3D model in SketchUp with a project’s Schedule in Programa.

    Programa’s Schedules function acts as a streamlined alternative to spreadsheets, detailing each item’s code, supplier, finish, dimensions, quantity and price.

    The extension runs inside SketchUp and allows designers to link components in the model to matching products in the Schedule.

    As a result, designers can track an item from the first 3D sketch through to its final specification, without entering the same information separately in SketchUp and Programa.

    From the model, designers can send a component to a chosen Schedule, or link it to a product that is already listed there.

    Programa explained that linking to an existing product creates a connection without adding a duplicate line item, keeping the Schedule “clean” as the design is fleshed out.

    Before anything is added, designers can review and edit the product’s information.

    The Schedule entry combines the details available from the component with anything entered during that review.

    Programa remarked this gives studios a chance to check the specification before it is used for pricing or procurement.

    The extension also provides access to Programa’s Product Library within SketchUp.

    Designers can place saved 3D models directly into their designs, and use product images as material swatches to bring selected finishes into the model.

    In this way, the products (and finishes) a studio has chosen can be seen in the visuals as well as listed in the Schedule.

    The process also works in reverse, starting from the Schedule. A product with a compatible 3D model attached can be placed straight into SketchUp.

    If there is no model, designers can choose a stand-in from SketchUp’s 3D Warehouse, or from elsewhere in the current model, to represent the product.

    Once a component and a product are connected, supported changes can be reviewed and applied in either direction.

    For example, adding another copy of a connected chair in SketchUp generates a quantity change, which the designer can then apply to the Schedule.

    The tech giant added that changes are presented for review “before the corresponding update is applied”.

    This means the model and the specification can move together as a design develops, while the Schedule is only updated once the designer has chosen to apply a change.

    Programa stressed that responsibility remains with the studio.

    Designers stay in charge of “selecting the right product, checking its details and deciding when the model or Schedule should change”, the company noted.

    The aim, it explained, is to carry information between the model and the specification rather than make those decisions on the designer’s behalf.

    The extension is aimed at studios that model in SketchUp and manage their specifications in Programa.

    The Programa extension works with SketchUp desktop on Mac and Windows.

    To learn more, visit Programa’s website or its extension setup guide.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Side stitch, stomach cramp, side ache — whatever you wanna call it, that mid-run pain in your tum can seriously *cramp* your runner’s high.

    This pesky prob that plagues runners and athletes all over has a scientific name: Exercise-related transient abdominal pain (ETAP). Though experts don’t know exactly what causes it, they have some ideas and tips about how to stop it.

    Before you double-over during your next marathon, here’s what to know.

    That fateful stab in your side is most likely to happen during exercise where your upper bod notes tight and upright for an extended period, such as when you run, jog, bike, hike, play soccer, etc.

    This common prob has been around for ages — the first historical mention is from ancient Roman philosopher Pliny the Elder. Yet, scientists still haven’t reached a consensus on its exact cause. We know that it affects up to 70% of runners each year.

    It’s also more likely to occur on the right side.

    A stiff spine or poor posture (according to older research from 2010) could contribute to side stitches – but TBH, the pros don’t know for sure.

    According to a 2022 review, researchers also think a side stitch might be caused by your right foot hitting the ground while you breathe out, irritating a phrenic nerve. Researchers think this, in turn, may bother the lining of your abdomen (particularly on the lower right side). Since most people are right-foot dominant, this is one possible explanation.

    Experts also theorize that it could be triggered by the boost of blood flow around the diaphragm when running.

    Furthermore, fueling up before a substantial race is excellent — but eating or drinking large quantities right before running may boost your risk of getting a side stitch, anecdotal reports suggest.

    When a side stitch strikes, don’t stress – there are steps you can take, including:.

    To stop a side stitch before it begins, here are some ideas FTW:.

    It has been revealed that side stitches are usually harmless. But it’s always a good idea to visit a pro if you experience any of the following probs:.

    According to recent reports, side stitches are a common matter and not typically the reason for concern. Though pros don’t know what causes them, they think problems with breathing, posture, or nerves may play a role.

    Consider working on your running form or breathing to reduce the risk of experiencing a side stitch. Staying hydrated and avoiding huge meals pre-run may also help. Consider working with a physical therapist or personal trainer if your problems persist.

    If you experience pain under your breastbone when running, visit a doctor asap.
